test_title: RRB ALP CBT-I 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 29 Nov, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Two trains travelling in the same direction at 40 km/h and 22 km/h cross each other completely in 1 minute. If the length of the first train is 125 m, what is the length of the second train?
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Relative speed (same direction) = 40 − 22 = 18 km/h

Convert to m/s: 18 × (5/18) = 5 m/s

Total distance (L₁ + L₂) = Speed × Time = 5 × 60 = 300 m

Length of second train = 300 − 125 = 175 m

**∴ The correct answer is 175 m.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of first train (S₁) = 40 km/h

Speed of second train (S₂) = 22 km/h

Time taken (t) = 1 min = 60 s

Length of first train (L₁) = 125 m

**Formula Used:**

Relative Speed (same direction) = S₁ − S₂

Total Distance = Length of Train 1 + Length of Train 2

Distance = Speed × Time

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/77450b43095b98e8bdc719b48a54b158d229fbaac622a53a32a93b18290b288c.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Relative Speed = (40 − 22) km/h = 18 km/h

⇒ Convert Speed to m/s = 18 × (5/18) = 5 m/s

⇒ Total Distance (L₁ + L₂) = Relative Speed × Time

⇒ 125 + L₂ = 5 × 60

⇒ 125 + L₂ = 300

⇒ L₂ = 300 − 125

⇒ L₂ = 175 m

**∴ The correct answer is 175 m.**

**__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed in Same Direction

When two objects move in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference of their individual speeds (S₁ − S₂).

Relative Speed in Opposite Direction

When two objects move towards each other, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds (S₁ + S₂).

Speed Unit Conversion

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.

Train Crossing Concepts

When a train crosses another train, the total distance covered is the sum of the lengths of both trains.</p
